newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eurometaux against EU classing metals as hazardous.
newsitem.headline: Eurometaux against EU classing metals as hazardous.

text.p: The European metals industry organisation Eurometaux will fight initiatives at the EU level to classify certain metals as hazardous waste and to curb their use, Werner Marnette, the new Eurometaux president said.

"Environmentally-inspired initiatives are afoot at the DG (Directorate General) XI to classify all base and precious metals," he said in an interview at the German copper smelter Norddeutsche Affinerie, where he chairs the board.
"This is with view to reducing their permissible use and regulating storage and transport."

"We're determined to fight this process because we as the industry already integrate metals into the recycling process in a controlled manner, which is environmentally conscious and aims to save energy."
"We also don't agree with the methods of testing metals properties for example in liquid rather than solid form and in environments untypical of metals use."
Marnette did not give a time schedule for possible EU moves, nor did he quantify the threat to consumption, but he said he had scheduled talks with the EU in order to be proactive.
Marnette has held the two-year post at Eurometaux since January 1, 1997, succeeding Italian industrialist Rosolino Orlando.
He said other planned areas of action were the harmonisation of environmental legislation affecting the metals industry and the promotion of metals use.
It was also planned to create closer links with the eastern European metals industry and to combat what Marnette called unfair distortions to international scrap trade flows.
